四级核心词汇 · 14英文原文

The Stone with Two Labels

贴着两张标签的石头 · 589 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A science institute prepared a lunar exhibition to mark a century of space research. A museum loan included a gray fragment with a label that said it came from the Moon. The older card underneath called it a piece of a model. Mina, a physicist, asked her lab students to examine both before printing the catalog. A genuine sample could help visitors picture a distant world. A mistaken label would teach them to trust the wrong kind of evidence.

2A student wanted to use the stone's color as proof. Mina brought a piece of ordinary iron and a disk cut from a similar gray substance. Side by side, all three looked alike. She asked the students to classify them by observable characteristics. They measured the density of the two loose samples. A small fraction of the gray disk was missing. They had to be careful when calculating its volume. Neither measurement told them where the borrowed fragment had come from.

3An experienced technician looked at the borrowed fragment under a microscope. A particle on its outer surface reflected light like a grain of paint. Acid could dissolve the paint, so she put the instrument away. Instead, she checked the institute's archive. A photo showed the original model in a vacuum chamber. A strip of tape on the model had exactly the same pattern as the mark on the fragment. That match changed the direction of the inquiry.

4The model used physics to illustrate an object's path in orbit. A gear could accelerate its rotating arm. The arm held an automatic lamp. A generator supplied the motor. In one phase of the demonstration, the lamp made the surface seem almost pure white. The students realized that light could influence its apparent color. They devised a critical test with a filter and a fixed lamp.

5A physicist asked whether the team wanted to explain relativity as well. Mina thought it would be better to conclude one inquiry clearly before introducing another concept. She wrote a logical sequence on a sheet. First observe the structure. Next formulate a prediction based on a theory. Then test it. At each step a visitor could reject an idea if the evidence contradicted it. That simple technique would leave more room for thought than a display full of theoretical terms.

6A comparative test could show a difference in density. It could not establish a history. The archive assistant, who specialized in geology, found multiple labels in the collection. The oldest gave the classification of a substance used to manufacture models. Its date and the photo gave them a more precise clue regarding origin.

7An old photograph finally revealed the fragment's origin. The label described a sample that had gone on display in the case next to the model. During a move someone had put its card beside the wrong item. A curator asked whether the model piece deserved a place in the exhibition. Mina said it had an important purpose. A visitor could compare an actual sample with a model without assuming that they were identical.

8On opening day a student used a microphone to explain the two labels. He held a replica of the gray disk rather than pointing to a remote image. A visitor asked which instrument had solved the mystery. He answered that the microscope had raised the question. The photograph had helped him answer it. The institute kept both labels to share that insight. What had looked like a small printing error had become a chance to see how scientific ideas evolve.

四级核心词汇 · 14中文译文

贴着两张标签的石头

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一所科学研究院筹办月球展，纪念太空研究走过一个世纪。博物馆借来一块灰色碎片，标签说它来自月球，下方那张更早的卡片却说它是模型的一部分。物理学家米娜请实验室里的学生在印目录前，把两张卡都查一遍。真正的样本能让参观者想象遥远的世界。一张错标签，也会教他们信错证据。

2一个学生想拿石头的颜色当证据。米娜带来一块普通的铁，又拿来一块用相似灰色材料切成的圆片。三样摆在一起，看起来差不多。她请学生根据能观察到的特征给它们分类。他们测了两件可取出来的样品的密度。灰色圆片缺了一小块，计算体积时得格外仔细。这两项测量都说明不了借来的碎片究竟出自哪里。

3一位经验丰富的技术员把借来的碎片放在显微镜下。外表面有个小颗粒，像一粒油漆一样反光。酸可能把漆溶掉，她便把仪器收起来，转去查研究院的档案。一张照片拍下了真空舱里的原模型。模型上有一段胶带，留下的图案和碎片上的痕迹完全一样。这个吻合让调查有了新方向。

4那件模型利用物理原理来说明物体沿轨道怎样运动。一个齿轮能让旋臂加快转动，旋臂上装着一盏自动灯，发电机给电机供电。演示进行到某一阶段时，灯把物体表面照得几乎纯白。学生发现，光会影响眼睛看到的颜色。他们用滤光片和固定的灯，设计了一次关键的测试。

5一位物理学家问，要不要顺便讲相对论。米娜认为，先把这一项调查讲明白，再引出另一个概念会更好。她在纸上写下清楚的顺序。先观察结构，再根据理论提出预测，然后做实验。每一步里，证据如果和想法矛盾，参观者都可以放弃原来的判断。用这么简单的办法，比摆满理论术语更能让人自己思考。

6对比试验可以看出密度的差别，却不能直接说明东西的来历。研究地质的档案助理在馆藏里找到好几张标签。年代最久的那张，记着制造模型用的一种材料该归到哪一类。上面的日期和照片一起，给了学生一条更准确的线索。

7一张旧照片最终揭示了碎片的来历。说它来自月球的标签，其实讲的是模型隔壁展柜里的一份样本。搬动展品时，有人把那张卡放到了错误物件旁。策展人问，模型碎片还有没有必要展出。米娜认为它有重要用途。参观者可以把真的样本和模型拿来比较，也就不用先假定它们是一回事。

8开幕当天，一个学生用麦克风介绍两张标签。他手里拿的是灰色圆片的复制品，大家不用远远地看一张图。有位参观者问，是哪件仪器解开的谜。学生说，是显微镜提出了问题，照片帮他找到了答案。研究院把两张标签都留下来，让别人也能看见这点。原先像个小小的印刷错误，如今成了一次观察科学想法怎样变化的机会。
